items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: Brown joined us in about January and we were down in Wichita and working... Brown knew nothing about music. He just left it up to us.

ctx.x: I wonder what -- let me make a note of that. I don't think -- I think they must have destroyed it.

Well, we recorded it, and they played it back for us and everything. But they said, no, this is a little far away from the picture we have of Jay McShann. We want some blues. So -- in fact, McShann -- we stayed in that studio and played it lots of things for them and they listened and told us to go back to the blues. In fact, if you notice, lots of things, you could probably tell that they were being made up right there (inaudible). Brown had the words as we went along.

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: Bird had gone over to Walter Brown's wife. Her name was Jean something -- Jean Brown

ctx.x: : Well, when -- now, there's -- I'm a little confused about when Bird leaves McShann.

Well now, there's -- we played the Savoy, as you know, and then we went into the Apollo and played that. And we went back into the Savoy, and we had an incident there on a Sunday afternoon. Bird had gone over to Walter Brown's wife. Her name was Jean something -- Jean Brown -- and she -- and had gotten Walter Brown's last $5.00 from his wife.
